name: Assyrian nationalism
summary: Assyrian nationalism holds that Assyrians, Chaldeans and Syriacs form one indigenous Mesopotamian nation whose identity transcends church divisions. It seeks recognition, equal citizenship, remembrance of the genocide and massacres, and autonomy or self-administration in the northern Mesopotamian homeland, centred today on the Nineveh Plains. Its mainstream institutional forms (the Assyrian Democratic Movement and the Assyrian Universal Alliance) frame the demand as autonomy within a democratic, federal Iraq rather than partition. It has little economic doctrine.
scope: The mainstream contemporary movement as expressed by the Assyrian Democratic Movement (Zowaa), the Assyrian Universal Alliance and the historical figures named in the Wikipedia article (Naum Faiq, Freydun Atturaya, Agha Petros). Excludes Chaldean or Syriac-only identity movements, and the non-Christian Pan-Mesopotamian variant is noted but not the basis. Most economic and social statements are not addressed by the movement, so many answers are low-confidence inferences.

sources.usedFor: Autonomy, minority election-law reform, minority inclusion in defence forces.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Nothing in Assyrian nationalist sources addresses health care; ADM's call for equality and post-ISIS reconstruction of basic infrastructure suggests mild support for public provision.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: No party text on wages was found, and the movement is a national-rights cause that spans employers and workers, so adherents are not pushed either way.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The movement has no economic doctrine; the Assyrian Democratic Organization's left-leaning past and diaspora business communities pull in opposite directions.

public-ownership.rationale: Some Assyrian movements were secular and left-leaning (s1) but economic ownership is not a defining demand, so this is split.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No stated tax position; the movement's concern is national rights rather than distribution, and adherents differ.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are not discussed in the sources; left-leaning strands might favour them but nationalist unity cuts across class lines.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property matters to the cause mainly as land: ADM objects to illegal encroachment on Christian-owned land, but there is no general doctrine of property rights.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Not addressed; reconstruction demands focus on state investment in the Nineveh Plains rather than corporate regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; a displaced, impoverished minority seeking state reconstruction aid is unlikely to favour welfare cuts.

worker-ownership.rationale: Only the left-leaning secular strand might support this; it is not part of the national programme.

surveillance-ok.rationale: No position found; a community targeted by ISIS terrorism may accept security measures, but minorities also fear state overreach.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; church-linked, socially conservative community norms suggest mild opposition.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: ADM wants laws that prevent persecution on any basis and cites exclusionary ideologies as the cause of massacres, which suggests support for legal limits.

strong-leader.rationale: The movement was formed against Ba'athist dictatorship and calls for a democratic pluralistic federal Iraq, so a strong leader bypassing gridlock is unattractive.

state-harmful.rationale: ADM seeks state-guaranteed equality, representation and protection, so the idea that the state is harmful and unnecessary runs against its demands.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have organised armed village defence units (Nineveh Plain Protection Units), so restricting gun ownership is not an obvious preference.

empower-police-military.rationale: ADM calls for incorporating minorities into national defence forces and for security in the Nineveh Plains, which implies a stronger local security apparatus.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; church-aligned social conservatism suggests mild opposition.

decide-locally.rationale: The Nineveh Plain governorate demand rests on decentralisation through governorates as a democratic principle, so adherents favour local decision-making.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal policy is not discussed in the sources.

traditional-family.rationale: Churches are central to Assyrian communal life (s1), implying mild social conservatism, though no party text states it.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; church-centred communities lean against, though secular diaspora members differ.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; the Assyrian churches oppose abortion, so adherents lean against.

more-religion-public.rationale: Split: the movement unites people across Christian churches but also has secular strands and a non-Christian Pan-Mesopotamian variant (s1).

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: ADM demands compensation, right of return and recognition for descendants of Simele victims, which is correcting historical injustice to an ethnic-religious group.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed in any source consulted.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Preserving Chaldean-Syriac-Assyrian culture, history and identity is a stated aim of ADM and the AUA.

gradual-change.rationale: No stated position; the movement seeks significant constitutional change (new governorate) but through legal channels.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; a diaspora-based people with a stake in migration and refugee return would not favour restricting it.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: AUA appeals to UN declarations and covenants and to UNPO for self-determination, suggesting reliance on international bodies.

nation-first.rationale: Assyrian nationalists put their people first but have no state; for a stateless minority reliant on outside protection the statement does not fit cleanly.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Having suffered genocide and displacement by ISIS, adherents petition outside powers for protection (AUA asked the US to push for a self-administered region).

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed; a national movement with a defined homeland leans against, but diaspora members have benefited from open migration.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Technology is absent from ADM and AUA statements, which deal with rights, return and security.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Energy policy never appears in Assyrian nationalist sources, so there is nothing to infer from.

revolution-justified.rationale: ADM took up armed struggle in 1982 against Ba'athist rule, but later works within elections and federal institutions, so adherents are split.

experts-over-public.rationale: The movement's democratic stance favours elected representation, but expert rule is never discussed.

central-planning.rationale: Not addressed; no source supports planning, and the movement operates in democratic institutions.

land-value-tax.rationale: Tax design is not a concern of the movement; its land demands are about title and return, not taxation.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance taxation is absent from the sources and adherents have no shared view.

basic-income.rationale: Income support is not discussed; adherents' views would follow their diverse economic outlooks.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trade protection is not a theme; the movement's economic demands are about regional reconstruction.

state-directs-investment.rationale: ADM asks for state-led reconstruction of the Nineveh Plains, but nothing speaks to strategic industries as such.

widespread-small-property.rationale: ADM defends village landholdings against encroachment, which fits small property, but there is no stated economic principle.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: No source suggests this; it is outside the movement's concerns.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions are outside the movement's concerns, so adherents are split or indifferent.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Wage-setting bodies are never raised; the movement organises by nation and church, not by occupation.

one-party-rule.rationale: ADM was founded against Ba'athist one-party rule and calls itself democratic, pluralist and federal.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Historic leaders such as Mar Shimun were patriarch-leaders and some early nationalists were royalist, but modern parties are republican and democratic; no stated view.

democracy-best.rationale: ADM describes itself as democratic and works for a democratic pluralistic federal Iraq; the 'even when voters choose badly' clause is a worry for a minority, so not the strongest.

direct-votes.rationale: No position on referendums; a small minority could be outvoted in them.

workers-councils.rationale: Not a position of the movement.

right-to-secede.rationale: ADM states it does not seek to divide Iraq, while some nationalists historically sought independence; the AUA frames its demand as autonomy.

natural-rulers.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's equality claims run against it.

political-violence-never.rationale: ADM's own armed struggle from 1982 and village defence forces mean adherents do not hold that violence is never justified.

war-builds-character.rationale: The movement's formative memory is genocide and massacre, so glorifying war is unlikely.

separate-church-state.rationale: Split: secular left strands exist (s1), yet the movement unites across churches and its identity is bound to Christian institutions.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Not an Assyrian nationalist demand; a Christian minority in Muslim-majority states wants equal civil law not religious law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: ADM seeks state defence integration and legal protection; privatised justice is alien to it.

military-superiority.rationale: Not applicable to a stateless people.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Assyrian nationalism defines the nation by ethnicity across churches (s1), yet ADM seeks a pluralist federal Iraq, so not strongly.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nationalism treats the nation, not class, as the main unit; left strands existed but this is not the doctrine.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Distribution is not addressed; ADM's equality demand concerns citizenship and rights, not outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Assyrian nationalists present Assyrians as the indigenous people of Mesopotamia and seek autonomy in their homeland.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Assyrians themselves seek redress from Britain's unmet promises, but the statement is general; no source discusses reparations from colonial powers.

civilizational-union.rationale: Assyrian nationalism contrasts itself with Arabism and Islamic unity (s1), so pan-religious union is not its aim.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The sources are about communal survival, not individual ethics, so no position follows.

duties-before-rights.rationale: No position; the movement emphasises group rights and equal citizenship.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental ethics are absent from the sources.

limit-population.rationale: A demographically shrinking minority fighting displacement would not favour limiting its population.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not a theme; reconstruction and development are sought.

human-enhancement.rationale: No position; church-linked communities may be wary but nothing is stated.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not discussed; a minority fighting for representation would distrust opaque rule by algorithms.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Digital privacy is not discussed by ADM or AUA.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement looks back to ancient Assyrian heritage and a lost homeland but pursues modern autonomy within federal Iraq, so it does not seek a restored order over progress.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The movement states no view on how policies should be judged; its demands are principled claims of national rights.

direct-action.rationale: ADM works through elections, parliament and petitions to bodies such as the European Parliament.

means-match-ends.rationale: No source discusses the relation of means to ends beyond ADM's turn from armed struggle to elections.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Wholly foreign to a movement that celebrates an ancient urban civilisation and seeks modern reconstruction.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Outside the movement's concerns and contrary to its development demands.

distribute-by-need.rationale: No stated position; left strands might lean in favour.

production-for-use.rationale: Economic organisation is not a theme, so adherents are indifferent or split.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Only the left-leaning strand might hold this; the national programme does not.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: ADM stands for democratic pluralist federalism; proletarian dictatorship has no place in it.

collective-farming.rationale: ADM defends villagers' own landholdings against encroachment, which cuts against collectivisation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not a nationalist claim; the movement blames chauvinist and exclusionary ideologies for massacres.

taxation-theft.rationale: ADM relies on state reconstruction funding and state guarantees, so a rejection of taxation is unlikely.

harm-principle.rationale: Limits on liberty are not debated in the sources; adherents' views would vary.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The movement claims collective rights for a people (autonomy, representation) alongside equal individual citizenship.

conscription.rationale: ADM wants minorities incorporated into national defence forces but sources are silent on compulsory service.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Assyrians have emigrated massively, but the movement wants representation and a homeland to stay in, so voice and political rights matter more.

state-as-business.rationale: Not discussed; equal-citizenship demands run against treating citizens as customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Material prerequisites of freedom are not discussed; ADM asks for reconstruction but not as a theory of freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Claims about media and universities are not part of the movement's discourse.

hereditarian-race.rationale: ADM stresses equal citizenship irrespective of nationality, belief or culture, so racial hierarchy claims are not part of it.

organic-representation.rationale: ADM seeks election-law changes for fair party representation of minorities, not corporatist bodies.

total-state.rationale: A minority that suffered state repression under Ba'athism opposes totalising states.

national-rebirth.rationale: Nationalist writers stress reviving Assyrian identity after the genocide, but the movement does not use a decadence narrative; inferred.

territorial-expansion.rationale: ADM says it does not seek to divide Iraq or build a state beyond its homeland, and a stateless minority cannot expand.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Contradicts the democratic federal order that ADM advocates.

bound-labor.rationale: Contradicts the equal citizenship ADM demands.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Epistemology is outside the movement, apart from complaints that Assyrian history was ignored in Iraqi accounts.

universal-morality.rationale: No stated position; the churches affirm universal morals, the movement itself is silent.

single-common-good.rationale: ADM favours pluralism and respects differences; no stated view on a single common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Assyrians' views are split and the movement takes no stated position, though a stateless people seeking a homeland may sympathise.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: ADM and the AUA press for the right of return of displaced Assyrians to their homeland and a reverse-migration trend is welcomed.

revive-national-language.rationale: Neo-Aramaic (Suret) is still spoken, so revival is not needed, but ADM promotes Syriac education and the AUA principle is one language for one nation; inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Company governance is not discussed; only the left strand could take this up.

school-vouchers.rationale: No stated position; Assyrians seek state support for Syriac-language and community schools, which could favour choice.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not discussed in any source consulted.

economic-freedom.rationale: The link between economic and political freedom is not addressed by the movement.

rule-by-example.rationale: The movement demands laws and institutions for protection rather than reliance on rulers' morality.

national-self-determination.rationale: The AUA aims at an autonomous state in the Assyrian homeland and cites international self-determination covenants, and the nationalism article describes a drive for independence or autonomy.

force-without-un.rationale: Not addressed; a stateless people has no such policy.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not stated; church-linked communities and a broad church-unity project lean against exclusive reason.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare eligibility is not discussed; a diaspora people has mixed interests on migrants' benefits.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare conditions are not discussed in the movement's sources.

class-collaboration.rationale: National unity across classes is central to nationalism, though adherents do not state a doctrine of class partnership.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Preserving Assyrian history and heritage is a core aim, and Assyrian sites were destroyed by ISIS.

workers-nation.rationale: Class is secondary to nation, but there is no stated doctrine on national workers' organisation; left strands differ.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: No position; church-aligned conservatism and secular strands conflict.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; no source indicates support, and Christian communities do not generally hold this.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Contradicts the equal citizenship ADM demands.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Left strands might agree; the national programme treats the state as an arena for minority rights, not a ruling-class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: No position, though Nineveh includes oil-rich Iraq; nothing stated.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: A minority fighting to preserve its own identity is unlikely to demand assimilation by others.

elite-replacement.rationale: ADM objects to demographic manipulation in the Nineveh Plains by local actors, which is a different claim from an elite plot of mass immigration.

proportional-representation.rationale: ADM calls for election-law reform guaranteeing fair political representation for minorities, which proportional or reserved seats serve.

national-mission.rationale: A movement for its own people's survival has no mission to spread its government elsewhere.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Gender structures are not addressed in the ADM or AUA material, which centres on ethnic persecution.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: ADM criticises both Baghdad and Erbil for failing to protect the community, but a general claim about elites is not stated.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: No support in the sources; incompatible with equality claims.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: ADM demands transparent investigation of the 2014 Baghdede genocide and justice for victims of Simele and Anfal.

night-watchman-state.rationale: ADM demands state-funded reconstruction, protection and equality laws.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Identity preservation across churches is a theme and endogamy is traditional, but no source supports discouragement by policy.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: ADM seeks equal citizenship regardless of nationality, belief, religion, culture or language.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Only for the left strand; not a nationalist doctrine.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The movement does not frame other states as settler colonies, and the topic is not covered.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Split: equal citizenship favours uniform law, yet minorities in Iraq seek their own personal-status arrangements.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Assyrian churches historically oppose proselytism across churches; no stated policy and Christians in Muslim states fear anti-conversion laws.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No relevance or support in the sources.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Split: secular strands favour; church communities want Christian instruction for their own children.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A democratic, pluralist movement does not endorse strengthening a socialist state.

consent-of-governed.rationale: ADM's democratic federal programme and its claim to self-rule rest on the consent of the governed.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist aims are absent; the movement has no state or trade policy of its own.

population-transfer.rationale: Assyrians have been the victims of forced removal, demographic manipulation and expulsion, and ADM opposes them.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: No stated position, and ADM's armed history means adherents are not absolutists.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Not a theme; the movement sees struggle between peoples as having produced massacre.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: No position; sufferers of chauvinist ideologies may favour it but minorities fear bans.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Inferred from demands for autonomy so that a people is not subject to the arbitrary power of Baghdad or Erbil.

separated-powers.rationale: ADM supports a federal pluralist state, which divides power vertically; no stated view on checks among bodies.

vanguard-party.rationale: Only left strands could hold it; not a nationalist doctrine.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Poverty is not framed as a priority; the movement's priorities are rights, return and security.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing policy with no echo in the movement's sources.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labour law is not part of the movement's demands.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The movement does not discuss causes of poverty; it stresses displacement and persecution.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: ADM emphasises pluralism and coexistence with other Iraqi communities.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not a theme; a minority seeks guaranteed elected representation.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: A minority persecuted by state repression opposes suspension of legal protections.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price policy is not in the sources, so adherents have no shared view.

party-controls-media.rationale: Contradicts the democratic pluralism ADM advocates.

party-commands-army.rationale: ADM calls for minorities to be integrated into national forces, i.e. state command; party command is contrary to its democratic stance.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation rules are not discussed, and a diaspora people has mixed interests.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Politicians' pay is not an issue in the movement's sources.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Internal party rules appear only as approved bylaws at ADM's conference, with no stated stance on binding discipline.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: No position, though Assyrian groups lobby European institutions.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Constitutional design of command is not addressed, apart from ADM's call to integrate minorities into national forces.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Assyrian churches are episcopal and the identity project works with church hierarchies, but the movement does not state a view on church governance.

clerical-rule.rationale: Clerical rule contradicts ADM's democratic programme and the nationalist critique that church leaders divide Assyrians.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Great-power war strategy is outside the movement's concerns.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed; democratic pluralism suggests opposition.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed; democratic stance suggests opposition.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall is not discussed; ADM seeks representation, not removal procedures.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Assyrian groups seek protection from outside powers rather than withdrawal of foreign forces.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: No relation to the movement's demands.

people-in-arms.rationale: The movement has raised village defence forces, but ADM also asks for inclusion in national forces.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Villages are the heart of the homeland claim, but no stated moral view on rural life.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not a theme; nationalist movements are historically led by educated intelligentsia such as Naum Faiq.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: ADM emphasises pluralism and respect for differences.

death-penalty.rationale: Capital punishment is not addressed by the movement; adherents' views are mixed.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Curriculum policy on sex education is not covered, and secular and church strands would differ.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not a theme and unlikely to be supported by secular strands.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; church-influenced views may favour limits but nothing is stated.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: A diaspora nation seeking return of its people favours descent-based ties; inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: ADM is credited with developing Syriac-language education and demands minority recognition and rights.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions from general laws are not discussed, though a religious minority might welcome them.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill-style individuality is not a theme; a minority preserving communal identity is split on it.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Foreign debt is not mentioned in the sources.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The left strand might agree; the programme concentrates on political autonomy.

constituent-assembly.rationale: ADM works within Iraq's constitution (Article 125) rather than calling for a new one.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: ADM asks for post-ISIS reconstruction aid; general global aid is not discussed.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Not applicable to a stateless people.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The movement states no view on how heads of state are chosen.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banking never appears in the sources.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not addressed directly; homeland attachment suggests lean yes but the movement accepts federal compromise.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: No source addresses the justification of property beyond defending villagers' land.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A debate internal to Marxism that the movement does not engage with.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation is not discussed by the movement.

collective-defense.rationale: Assyrian groups seek outside guarantees of protection; inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Assyrian nationalists have seen annexation of Hakkari highlands as lost, but no stated position on this principle.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The movement's critics of clergy want national identity before church, but the movement does not seek subordination of churches.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The ceremonial role of a head of state is not discussed; Iraq's presidency is not a movement issue.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Assyrians have suffered state repression and do not endorse forcing regions to stay, though ADM itself stays federal.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The Nineveh Plain governorate demand and AUA's self-administered region are autonomy within a larger state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: No support; incompatible with the democratic programme.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax rate structure is absent from the sources.

character-from-environment.rationale: The nature-nurture question is not discussed, though the movement believes identity can be revived through education.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: A persecuted minority and democratic party opposes rulers above the law.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy has no connection to the movement's concerns.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is not discussed by the movement.

leader-cult.rationale: Ba'athist leader cults were a target of the movement.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court policy is not discussed in the sources.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A question for Marxist-Leninist theory that the movement does not address.

land-redistribution.rationale: ADM wants land taken by encroachment returned to Christian owners, but not general redistribution.

refugee-return.rationale: ADM calls for right of return and compensation for displaced Assyrian villagers and descendants of Simele victims.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Assyrian claims are to a homeland within Iraq and neighbours, not claims on neighbouring states; no stated position.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not Assyrian doctrine; opposes forced religious dress.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not discussed; Assyrian parties lobby European bodies but state no currency view.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Assyrian nationalism unites Assyrians across churches and states, but a union of kin peoples across borders is not stated.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: ADM and the AUA seek a self-administered area and culture and language institutions; the AUA wants more than cultural autonomy, so only partly.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: AUA seeks an autonomous homeland, while ADM works for equal rights in Iraq; the statement's either-or splits the movement, with homeland aim stronger.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Nationalism treats identity and nation as drivers of history; only the left strand would stress material conditions.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not discussed in the sources.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are not discussed; there is no shared view.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: A minority seeking protection and guaranteed representation depends on courts and institutions constraining majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: No position found; mixed with church-aligned conservatism.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: No support in the sources; a diaspora people with global links.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade-agreement standards are not discussed in the sources.

moral-incentives.rationale: Incentive systems for labour are not part of the movement's sources.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: ADM's armed struggle was defensive and aimed at protecting villages and later joined democratic opposition.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Historic patriarchal leadership was hereditary (Mar Shimun), but no current stated position.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Teaching Assyrian history is central; nationalists revived ancient Assyria as heritage.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Assyrians experienced British and Ottoman domination; the doctrine is contrary to self-determination.

patriotic-education.rationale: Nationalists promote teaching Assyrian identity, language and the flag, though loyalty to a state is distinct.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The movement seeks minority representation, which is not the same as affirmative action in admissions or hiring, so it states no view.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is absent from the sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Capitalist crisis theory is absent from the movement's sources.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The ancient empire is a source of heritage but the movement has no imperial ambitions.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not a position of the movement.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: A persecuted minority seeking equal citizenship opposes freedom to discriminate.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: ADM seeks constitutional guarantees such as Article 125 and equality laws, which entrench minority rights.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Assyrians were divided by border settlements and British promises unfulfilled, suggesting sympathy; no source states the principle.

minority-veto.rationale: ADM wants guaranteed representation, but there is no stated claim of a veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: ADM took up arms against Ba'athist dictatorship and treats massacres as state crimes; inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: ADM sits in parliament and appeals to parliament for equality laws.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is not discussed by the movement.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not discussed; no shared position can be inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Duties of the wealthy are not stated; diaspora philanthropy for the homeland is a practice, not a doctrine.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: A movement built on political action.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A Frankfurt-school claim the movement does not engage with.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony theory is not part of the movement's thought.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is not part of the movement's sources.

native-born-offices.rationale: No position, though a diaspora people would be wary.

party-own-road.rationale: Relations among communist parties are irrelevant to the movement.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: ADM asks for outside reconstruction support.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Nationalists mourn the lost Hakkari highlands but no stated demand to retake them.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Assyrians claim indigenous status but ADM seeks equal citizenship in a pluralist state, not leadership over others.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Constitutional anti-fascism is not discussed in the sources.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Comparisons of fascism and communism are not part of the movement's discourse.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument debates do not appear in the sources, though adherents care about preserving Assyrian heritage sites.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The movement seeks democratic institutions; a minority gains little from exemptions from Western norms.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Assyrians were repressed by the Iraqi army (Simele); ADM favours democratic order.

paid-care-work.rationale: Care work is not discussed in the sources.

filial-duty.rationale: Family and community obligations are strong in Assyrian communities; inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil-service recruitment is not discussed; ADM seeks proportional representation instead.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Strategic industry control is not discussed in the sources.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Church-aligned norms lean against; no source states it.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Imperative mandates are not discussed in the sources.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is absent from the sources.

land-use-tenure.rationale: ADM defends community and private title in villages against seizure.

single-official-language.rationale: A movement defending Syriac language rights opposes suppression of other languages; Iraq's Ba'athist Arabisation harmed Assyrians.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: ADM objects to land encroachment and demographic manipulation by outsiders, but no explicit position on foreigners.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: A US-law notion that the movement does not address.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumption ethics are absent from the sources.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Not applicable to a stateless people; the movement was itself an insurgent group.

corporate-influence.rationale: Lobbying and campaign finance are not part of the movement's concerns.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Assyrian organisations depend on diaspora and foreign funds and would oppose restrictions.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: A shrinking minority concerned by emigration and demographic change would favour measures to keep and increase its numbers.

residents-only-property.rationale: ADM demands protection of Nineveh Plains land from demographic manipulation and purchases by outsiders.

job-guarantee.rationale: Employment guarantees are not discussed, though ADM asks for job creation in the Nineveh Plains.

democratic-peace.rationale: International relations theory is not discussed by the movement.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Political obligation is not discussed in the sources.

non-intervention.rationale: Assyrian groups ask outside powers, the UN and the US, to push for their rights.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is outside the movement's concerns.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: A persecuted minority rejects conspiracy claims against minorities.

public-access-to-information.rationale: ADM demands transparent investigation of the Baghdede genocide.

local-production.rationale: Local-economy ideals are not discussed beyond village reconstruction.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement builds parties, federations and a worldwide alliance.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Assyrian groups rely on international covenants and declarations in their claims.

religious-nation.rationale: Assyrian nationalism seeks to unite across churches under an ethnic identity, and a Pan-Mesopotamian variant is independent of Christianity.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tributary diplomacy has no link to the movement's sources.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from the push for governorate autonomy and local reconstruction funding.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Marxist property theory is not part of the movement's sources.

defeat-communism.rationale: No position, though the ADO's left strand diverges.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Service-delivery models are not discussed in the sources.

religion-illusion.rationale: The movement works through Christian churches and respects religious pluralism.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Assessment of capitalism's historical role is absent from the sources.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Feminist economic theory is not part of the movement's sources.

socialized-care.rationale: Public provision of domestic work is not discussed by the movement.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Nationalist language revival may stress Aramaic purity but no source is read.

treaties-binding.rationale: Assyrians cite broken Allied promises and treaties; inferred preference for binding commitments.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Not a position of the movement.

majority-settlement.rationale: ADM opposes demographic manipulation and settlement of other groups in Nineveh Plains, where Assyrians are a minority.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Assyrians claim indigenous roots in northern Mesopotamia as the basis of the homeland demand.

holocaust-denial.rationale: A people that was the victim of genocide and demands recognition rejects genocide denial.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not a position of the movement, though church-aligned views are conservative.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Contradicts democratic pluralism and the movement's history under Ba'athism.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: A Christian minority has suffered under blasphemy laws and rejects this.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Assyrians experienced British Mandate policy and oppose colonial domination.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not part of the Christian movement; Assyrian groups were targeted by jihadist forces such as ISIS.

participatory-democracy.rationale: ADM emphasises representation and parliamentary routes, and the sources do not mention workplace or participatory forms.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectional analysis is not part of the movement's discourse, which centres on ethnic-religious persecution.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: No stated position; the movement spans left and centre.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist alienation theory is not part of the movement's sources.

islam-incompatible.rationale: ADM calls for coexistence with other Iraqi communities and national and religious pluralism.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: ADM's source of authority is the people in a democratic Iraq; church identity is separate.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Religious dress rules are not addressed by the movement.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Workplace-law policy is not discussed by the movement.

social-market-economy.rationale: Economic system choice is not discussed by the movement.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: ADM calls for minorities in defence forces, and a defence militia exists.

rich-first.rationale: Development sequencing is not discussed in the sources.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Alliance policy for a stateless people is not a question the sources address.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Contradicts the democratic programme, though the patriarchate was hereditary in the Mar Shimun line.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Alternative banking is not discussed in the sources.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: IMF conditionality is not discussed in the sources.

property-franchise.rationale: Equal citizenship contradicts property limits on the vote.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist theory is not part of the movement's discourse.

reification.rationale: Marxist theory of commodity fetishism is not part of the movement's sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Press ownership is not discussed in the sources.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: ADM demands equality laws and legal protection.

online-participation.rationale: Digital democracy is not discussed in the sources.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Church-bound communal endogamy, but nothing stated; minorities fear restrictions imposed on them.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: A persecuted minority rejects boycott of minorities.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition assemblies are not discussed in the sources.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Church doctrinal reform is not a stated aim of the movement, and adherents are divided across several churches.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Wealth concentration is not discussed in the sources.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Not Assyrian doctrine, whose identity includes the churches, and the movement rejects state repression of religion.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: ADM asks for security and justice from state institutions.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: ADM demands political partnership and fair representation for minorities, so executive power sharing suits it.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: ADM asks the state for reconstruction.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not discussed; adherents have no shared position.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not discussed in the sources.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Existential risk is not discussed in the sources.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Assyrian churches do not ordain women; not a movement demand.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Marital authority is not discussed; church-influenced and secular strands may differ.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: A diaspora people would favour migrant voting rights; inferred.

rent-control.rationale: Housing rents are not discussed by the movement.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The Assyrian homeland is split among Iraq, Syria, Turkey and Iran and the nationalism article describes a drive for one homeland, but ADM works inside Iraq's federation, so support is moderate and inferred.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Recognition of the Sayfo and Simele and justice for the 2014 killings is central to Assyrian demands.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: the movement has little economic doctrine and no sources hold a view on intellectual property.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The mainstream movement seeks democratic, federal autonomy; drilled youth movements are not a theme. Inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: The movement does not address nuclear basing; no clear position can be inferred.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The sources do not address bases, and a vulnerable minority may welcome outside protection; no position can be inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The summary notes little economic doctrine, so there is no stated position.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The movement stresses protection of a community that suffered massacres and has sought self-defence forces; inferred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Assyrian nationalism holds that Assyrians are the indigenous descendants of ancient Mesopotamia, with a continuous identity from the ancient Assyrians.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred: the churches that anchor the community are traditional on this and the movement says nothing on it.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred: not addressed by the movement.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Assyrians commemorate the genocide and the Simele massacre of 1933 with official days of remembrance and call the dead martyrs.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The movement frames its aims in terms of rights, autonomy and democracy, not a cosmic struggle; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The movement seeks autonomy in the northern Mesopotamian homeland, especially the Nineveh Plains, as a place for the people to live, not merely a symbolic centre.

culture-before-state.rationale: The movement's demand is for political self-administration in the homeland, pursued alongside cultural preservation; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Assyrian churches use traditional liturgical language and adherents' view is inferred, not stated.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from the traditional churches that anchor the community; not addressed by the movement.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The movement seeks equal citizenship for a minority, which cuts against majority economic reservation; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The movement's main demand is a single autonomous region for the Assyrian, Chaldean and Syriac people in the Nineveh Plains.

independent-unions.rationale: The sources do not address labour organisation; no basis to lean.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The movement has little economic doctrine and does not frame itself in working-class terms.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Post-ISIS reconstruction of basic services in the Nineveh Plains is a movement priority, so public provision is mildly inferred.

second-chamber.rationale: The movement seeks autonomy within federal Iraq and has no stated position on legislative chambers.

municipal-property.rationale: The movement is not socialist and its autonomy demand concerns administration of territory, not communal ownership of production.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The movement seeks a governorate with its own administration rather than a municipal confederation; inferred from its autonomy demands.

person-over-state.rationale: Its demands for equal citizenship and justice for victims imply the individual is not to be sacrificed to the state; inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The movement is rooted in a shared Christian heritage and church identity, so a spiritual dimension is inferred.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The movement wants a self-administered region within Iraq, but does not specify whether its powers should be revocable.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The nation is defined by shared Mesopotamian heritage and language across denominations; organising around race is not its framing, so inferred as disagreement.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in ancient Assyrian ancestry and heritage is central to the movement's identity, though framed as national heritage rather than race.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Its stated aims are autonomy and justice by political means within Iraq, with no aggressive aims; defensive use is inferred.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The Assyrian Universal Alliance's stated aim is one language for one nation, and the movement unites Chaldeans, Syriacs and Assyrians under one identity across churches.

communal-electorates.rationale: The ADM demands reform of the minority election law so that Assyrians choose their own representatives, rather than having quota seats filled by others' votes.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The mainstream ADM opposes partition of Iraq and frames its goal as autonomy; it does cite great-power betrayal after the First World War but does not claim current plots. Inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: The movement has little economic doctrine and does not address tuition; inferred to be neutral.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not addressed; the movement has no environmental or economic programme to infer from.

future-generations.rationale: Preserving the homeland and heritage for descendants is a recurring theme; a general duty to future generations is inferred.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; inferred to be neutral.

arms-reduction.rationale: As a minority victimised by massacres and seeking protection through internationally backed autonomy, it leans toward multilateral peace and security; inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The movement appeals to international bodies and treaty guarantees such as the Paris and Lausanne claims, and favours transparency over secret deals that betrayed it; inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: The movement has no economic doctrine and does not address capital flows; inferred to be neutral.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: ADM calls for minority inclusion in defence forces and local security for the Nineveh Plain, implying support for community-based protection forces beside the state.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: A movement shaped by genocide and the need for self-defence is inferred to favour soldiers' duty to defend; interstate war refusal is not discussed.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The ADM platform stresses equality and social justice but no source addresses bargaining; mild support is inferred.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from ADM's equal-citizenship and reconstruction demands; economic policy is not addressed.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The movement has little economic doctrine and the sources never mention fiscal rules, so there is no basis for a lean.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The movement's concerns are minority rights and autonomy in Iraq, not international economic rules.

smash-state-machine.rationale: ADM seeks equal citizenship and autonomy within a democratic, federal Iraq and rejects partition, so it works through the existing state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The movement states no economic blueprint; autonomy might permit local choices but this is not addressed.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Environmental or resource valuation does not feature in Assyrian nationalist sources.

sacred-nation.rationale: Assyrian nationalism treats the Assyrians as one continuous Mesopotamian nation over millennia, whose identity transcends churches and is remembered through the genocide.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; no basis for a lean.

internal-colonialism.rationale: ADM complains of marginalisation and demographic change imposed on the Nineveh Plain by stronger central and regional powers, which parallels the claim, though wealth is not the issue stressed.

shared-human-nature.rationale: ADM's equal-citizenship and rights demands imply universal dignity; human nature itself is not discussed.

public-service-media.rationale: ADM's call for Syriac-language education and recognition implies support for publicly funded minority-language provision; media is inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred from the Christian character of Assyrian identity, where churches hold their own doctrines, though the movement says the nation transcends church divisions.

farm-price-support.rationale: The movement has little economic doctrine, so farm support is neither endorsed nor opposed in the sources.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The movement has no state of its own and does not address nuclear policy, so there is nothing to infer from beyond general silence.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Assyrian Democratic Movement is a national movement that spans classes and denominations, so a class-based workers' party runs against its framing.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the movement's democratic and human-rights framing; the sources do not discuss female genital cutting.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the movement's commitment to equal citizenship and democracy; the sources do not discuss inheritance.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred from the movement's insistence that Assyrians, Chaldeans and Syriacs are one people under one name, which extends to their shared Neo-Aramaic language.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from the movement's democratic institutionalism, which looks to state law and agencies; the sources do not address pollution.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The movement seeks democratic autonomy through elected bodies such as a Nineveh Plains governorate, so formal chiefly lawmaking roles are not part of its program; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The movement has no stated position on trading liberty against the environment.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The movement does not address sentencing policy.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from its civic federal-Iraq framing and cultural concern for language; the sources do not address immigrant language rules.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Not addressed: the movement has little labour doctrine and no stated stance on union membership rules.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; its concerns are recognition and autonomy, and adherents have no common view on voting procedure.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from its demand for equal citizenship and recognition of a community spanning several churches in a plural Iraq; not stated for religious interpretations as such.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred from its framing of autonomy within a democratic, federal Iraq; the sources do not define democracy procedurally.

premarital-sex.rationale: Not addressed; a community identity movement spanning conservative churches, so adherents are split.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from its democratic, rights-based framing and its experience of state repression; not addressed in the sources.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; the movement has little economic doctrine.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from its demand for equal citizenship and democratic participation; sex equality in voting is not discussed in the sources.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred: the movement is closely tied to the churches and treats religion as part of national heritage, so it would reject this.

race-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; Assyrian identity is framed as ethnic and historical, which sits uneasily with calling race a construct.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; adherents are likely split.

missingStatements.text: A people that is a minority in the state it lives in should have an autonomous self-governed province within that state.
missingStatements.rationale: ADM and the AUA demand a Nineveh Plain governorate or an Assyria province within Iraq with its own administration.

missingStatements.text: Governments should formally recognise past mass killings of a people as genocide.
missingStatements.rationale: Recognition of the Sayfo and Simele and justice for the 2014 killings is central to Assyrian demands.

missingStatements.text: The several religious denominations of a people should be united under one national identity.
missingStatements.rationale: The movement's defining aim is one Assyrian identity across Chaldean, Syriac and Church of the East communities.
missingStatements.declined: Uniting denominations under one identity is specific to this movement.

notes: Chaldean, Syriac and Assyrian labels are contested; the Chaldean Church rejects a unified identity. ADM leans toward Baghdad and other parties toward the KRG. A secular left strand and a non-Christian Pan-Mesopotamian variant would answer religion questions differently.
